question: Does the exact exhaustive NCC path (sliding integer window sums, eight-window UDOT products) speed up the stable core's fixed-scale match, with bit-identical outputs?

before.source: git archive of 65b7dad (UDOT rows, NEON rotation, frozen copy)
before.ncc: binary64 integral images, row-by-row dot products

after.source: worktree with the exhaustive NCC change
after.ncc: exact uint32 column sums slid to window sums; UDOT builds take products of eight adjacent windows over a zero-padded template; bounded/screened maps keep the original path

toolchain: Apple clang 21.0.0, CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release, FPM_WITH_OPENCV=ON, default target-cpu apple-m1 for both builds
benchmark_modes: cpp-core/tools/benchmark_modes.py --repeats 9 (one warm-up + 9 measured per mode, fresh process each); sessions interleaved before,after x3; the before sessions run the frozen base copy of the script
control: legacy_cpp mode is the same macos-cli/match_core.cpp binary in both builds
fixture_ab: cpp-core/tools/benchmark_backend_ab.py --rounds 8 (round 0 warm-up discarded), alternating order, 17 compare_versions cases
metric: fpm_cli match_ms (excludes image decoding and learning); no runs dropped or rerun
acceptance: speed is reported, not gated; identity is gated separately (check_backend_identity.py 544 runs, compare_versions.py, core_test exact-reference tests)
selection_history: pilot 1 (four-row interleaved window kernel plus uint64 integral images) and pilot 2 (this design) were compared on nine fixtures with 5 measured runs each before registration; pilot numbers are selection-only
profiling: instrumented and sample-based profiles are separate runs and are not formal timings
environment_note: other Claude/Codex sessions may be active on this machine; load averages are recorded per session
